fn-weather-03.front: Halo around the sun or moon means?
fn-weather-03.back: Thin cirrostratus, often ahead of a warm front: rain or snow within about a day.

fn-weather-06.front: Thunder heard: what do you do?
fn-weather-06.back: Go to a hard topped vehicle or building and wait 30 minutes after the last thunder.

fn-weather-09.front: Where does the Hunt Map show pressure trend?
fn-weather-09.back: Weather and wind sheet: rising, falling or steady over the last 3 hours.

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" role="img" aria-label="Buys Ballot's law: stand with your back to the wind in the northern hemisphere and low pressure is on your left, high pressure on your right.">
<rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="300" rx="0" fill="#dfe6d3" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="14" y="26" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="start" font-weight="bold">Back to the wind: low on your left</text><g transform="translate(200 200) scale(1.3)"><circle cx="0" cy="-30" r="7" fill="#2f3a2b"/><path d="M0 -23 V2 M0 2 L-7 18 M0 2 L7 18 M0 -16 L-9 -4 M0 -16 L9 -4" stroke="#2f3a2b" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round" fill="none"/></g><line x1="200" y1="280" x2="200.0" y2="232.7" stroke="#4a7fb0" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round"/><polygon points="200.0,225.0 193.9,236.0 206.1,236.0" fill="#4a7fb0"/><line x1="150" y1="285" x2="150.0" y2="247.7" stroke="#4a7fb0" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/><polygon points="150.0,240.0 143.9,251.0 156.1,251.0" fill="#4a7fb0"/><line x1="250" y1="285" x2="250.0" y2="247.7" stroke="#4a7fb0" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/><polygon points="250.0,240.0 243.9,251.0 256.1,251.0" fill="#4a7fb0"/><text x="260" y="275" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#4a7fb0" text-anchor="start" font-weight="bold">wind at your back</text><circle cx="70" cy="140" r="34" fill="#f4d9c4" stroke="#c92a2a" stroke-width="3"/><text x="70" y="150" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" fill="#c92a2a" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">L</text><text x="30" y="200" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#c92a2a" text-anchor="start">Low pressure,</text><text x="30" y="216" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#c92a2a" text-anchor="start">bad weather side</text><circle cx="330" cy="140" r="34" fill="#e8f2e0" stroke="#8a9a6b" stroke-width="3"/><text x="330" y="150" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" fill="#8a9a6b" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">H</text><text x="300" y="200" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#8a9a6b" text-anchor="start">High</text>
</svg>

fn-weather-11.front: Clear calm night: where does cold air go?
fn-weather-11.back: Down the slopes into the valley: fog and frost below (Tip: glass from above).
fn-weather-11.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" role="img" aria-label="At night cold air drains down the slopes and pools in the valley, making fog, frost and cold. On the slope above the fog it is often milder and clear. Tip: glass from above the fog.">
<rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="300" rx="0" fill="#e7f0f7" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="14" y="26" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="start" font-weight="bold">Cold air pools in valleys at night</text><path d="M0 120 L90 80 L170 200 L230 200 L300 70 L400 110 L400 300 L0 300 Z" fill="#c9d3b8" stroke="#8b5a2b" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-linecap="round"/><path d="M120 140 L170 200 L230 200 L285 120 Z" fill="#ffffff" stroke="none" stroke-width="0" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-dasharray=" opacity=".85""/><text x="200" y="175" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#4a7fb0" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">Fog, frost, cold</text><g transform="translate(330 82) scale(0.6)"><circle cx="0" cy="-30" r="7" fill="#2f3a2b"/><path d="M0 -23 V2 M0 2 L-7 18 M0 2 L7 18 M0 -16 L-9 -4 M0 -16 L9 -4" stroke="#2f3a2b" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round" fill="none"/></g><text x="190" y="48" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#e8590c" text-anchor="start" font-weight="bold">Glass from above</text><text x="190" y="64" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#e8590c" text-anchor="start" font-weight="bold">the fog (Tip)</text><line x1="60" y1="95" x2="104.8" y2="144.3" stroke="#4a7fb0" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/><polygon points="110.0,150.0 107.1,137.8 98.1,145.9" fill="#4a7fb0"/><line x1="350" y1="110" x2="296.4" y2="145.7" stroke="#4a7fb0" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/><polygon points="290.0,150.0 302.5,148.9 295.8,138.9" fill="#4a7fb0"/><text x="20" y="250" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#4a7fb0" text-anchor="start" font-weight="bold">Cold air drains down</text><text x="20" y="268" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#4a7fb0" text-anchor="start" font-weight="bold">slopes after sunset</text>
</svg>

fn-weather-12.front: How much colder per 1,000 m up?
fn-weather-12.back: About 6.5 degrees Celsius in standard air.
fn-weather-12.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" role="img" aria-label="A valley at 400 metres is 8 degrees Celsius. A ridge 1,000 metres higher is about 1.5 degrees: standard air cools about 6.5 degrees per 1,000 metres. Rain in the valley can be snow on the ridge.">
<rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
<text x="20" y="32" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="start" font-weight="bold">Higher is colder</text><path d="M20 270 L140 200 L230 90 L300 60 L380 140 L380 270 Z" fill="#c9d3b8" stroke="#8b5a2b" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-linecap="round"/><circle cx="40" cy="262" r="6" fill="#2f3a2b" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="50" y="250" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="start" font-weight="bold">Valley 400 m: 8°C</text><circle cx="260" cy="75" r="6" fill="#2f3a2b" stroke="none" stroke-width="2"/><text x="130" y="50" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#e8590c" text-anchor="start" font-weight="bold">Ridge 1,400 m: about 1.5°C</text><text x="20" y="295" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#868e96" text-anchor="start">About 6.5°C colder per 1,000 m up (standard air).</text>
</svg>

fn-weather-13.front: 8 degrees at a 400 m valley. Ridge at 1,400 m?
fn-weather-13.back: About 1.5 degrees. Rain below can be snow above.

fn-weather-14.front: Sitting still, your barometric altimeter climbs. Why?

fn-weather-15.back: Rain or snow soon. Folklore that fits the halo science.
